Valve Defaults Back To Showing All Reviews on Steam
You had one job Valve ONE fucking job.

Yeah, this had to happen. To many people don't buy through steam but activate through steam. A better process is to have devs pre-register their key ranges for reviewers. Then all reviews tied to those product keys are tied to a flag that says 'received a free copy of the game.'

Exactly. I had some dumbass get mad when I pointed out that a large number of gamers buy keys on cheaper sites and redeem them on Steam and this new policy was removing their reviews as well as paid reviews. Maybe he was just mad that he's never used other stores to buy games significantly cheaper?

Looking at several games in my library, "large number" seems like less than 10% (dramatically less than 10% for most games) of posted reviews.

It seems that there is a minority that buy through third party (and gray-market) retailers and redeem on steam, but that they're far more vocal than the majority that simply buy through steam. That, or they disproportionately choose not to review games.
Look at any game in Steam. The majority of people don't leave reviews, regardless of how they get the game.

Right, but when you talk about reverting a change like this because of impact on reviews by key redemption owners, you have to take into account the actual impact. The only metric for this is the ratio of key redemption reviews to steam purchase reviews.

Unarguably, if the ratio is small-- say, 10% or lower -- then the impact of excluding those reviews will be minimal. For most of the games I've looked at, the ratio is on that scale or smaller.

I'm of the impression that Valve reverted the change because the key redemption user base is simply vocal enough to make it seem like a bad PR move. They ultimately have better metrics than "looked at a dozen or so store pages of games I own", but that's my impression.

And Gabe caves... It was only a matter of time, really. Do yourself a favor and ignore the positive reviews; just look at the negatives. Why do you care about the positives? If you've come far enough to look at the reviews, then you already know why you want the game; you're there to figure out why you might not want the game.
I'm glad. I am a reviewer sometimes getting free keys, but I am not asked to give positive reviews. On the contrary, I can be pretty negative and point out the issues I see in the game.

Daily Devotional

September 21

1 Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not. 2 Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is. (1 John 3:1-2 KJV)

What an amazing thing God has done, to not only forgive us of our sins and bring us back into fellowship with Him, but to adopt us as sons. Being a son of God means that we are heirs of God as is Jesus (Romans 8:17), and that is hard for us born again Christians to get our minds wrapped around. It would have been wonderful to just be forgiven our sins, but to be adopted as sons, is beyond our expectations. If we are living our Christian lives, as we should, then the world will not understand us any better then it understood Jesus (John 15:20). If you are liked and understood by all the people in this world, then you are not letting Jesus live through you, as Paul said we should.

We have the promise of our bodies becoming like Jesus is now, and when we see Him face to face, we will be like Him, and know all things as He does (1 Corinthians 13:12). The Christian should certainly look forward to the day when we see Jesus, as it will be such a glorious time, to not only be with Him, but to begin our lives in a incorruptible body with Jesus and the Father forever – Hallelujah!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
